description_en: The monument is located on the northern part of the Dullu hilltop (Ward #8). It is found 400 meters south of the Baleśvara Mandir (DLK0340).The monument is a free-standing two-storied construction built in the fashion of Kathmandu valley, with brick walls and Newar style carved pillars and windows. A central bay with wooden pillars marks the entrance. Two small terracotta plates with erotic scenes on it are inserted in the facade's masonry. The vestibule leads to a single, central door. The wooden doorframe appears to be old (1819?), but it is heavily covered with brown paint. The wooden door panels are of more recent origin and displays more local decorative motifs. To the left of this door is a small terracotta figure of a standing Gaṇeśa. To the right of the door is an inscribed stone slab inserted in the masonry. The inscription contains the monument's date of construction, 'śake 1741' (1819 CE).Passed the central door is a rectangular room. To the north is a room where computers have been installed but solely used due to maintenance issues and lack of electricity. To the south is a metal staircase leading to the upper floor. At the centre of the rectangular room is a door leading to a recently walled back courtyard.The upper floor is a single, large room used as a museum. Shelves and tables have been installed to showcase various types of objects, mainly everyday objects related to agricultural work. There are also objects such as waterpipes (hukkā), drums, vessels, etc.According to the inscription situated next to the entrance door, the monument was built in 1819 (ŚS 1741, VS 1876), during the reign of King Rājendra Śāha (r. 1816-1846). The monument's was built as apauvā, a place for distributing water to travellers, which also provided them with a place to rest. In 2011 Bishwo K. C. Pokharel noted that the building was in a poor state of conservation and that the upper floor was used as restrooms (Pokharel 2011 [VS 2068], pp. 145-146). The situation has changed since then, with the municipality of Dullu having invested in the conservation of the place.
references: Sources and references Inscription identification number DLK0420_I Sources Pokharel, Bishwo K. C. 2011 [VS 2068]. Kīrtikhamba . Kathmandu: Prakāśka.

historical_events.event_description: An inscription on a stone slab placed on the right side of the door provides information about the monument's construction. The document is dated of  ŚS 1741 and VS 1876, which correspond to 1819 AD. It starts by naming the queen and king of Nepal (Rājendra Śāha, r. 1816-1846). The queen is mentioned as 'lakṣmīnārāyaṇadevatā'. It is probably Queen Samrajya Lakshmi Devi (c. 1814-1841), who was then five years old.Bishwo K. C.
